comments.body:
## DUPLICATE of [rebar:aec1-76e7-bb95-4c86] — that is the work ticket; this one's MECHANISM is the better half

Filed within minutes of each other for the same defect: I filed aec1 from the symptom (the c827
control-group question could not be answered from the store), and the c827 investigation filed this
one having found the actual cause. **aec1 is claimed and being implemented — work continues there.**

**This ticket's mechanism is the valuable part and has been handed to that implementation**, because
it converts a hypothesis into two concrete, testable defects:

* `usage_log.record()` **no-ops unless `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` is set** — unset by default, and unset here.
  So the recording code exists and is inert.
* `_FIELDS` (`usage_log.py:32`) records `requests` but **NOT `tool_calls`** — the one axis that
  separates a loop from genuine breadth, and the second of the two kill paths.

That is the same **computed-then-discarded** shape as its siblings — the repetition diagnostic built
by `interpret_failure` and dropped because `failure_diagnostic is None`, and the deterministic
child-closure proof collapsed to a boolean before it reaches the prompt
([rebar:6ec8-24c7-182b-40d0]). Three instances of one pattern in one subsystem.

Left open rather than closed: closing it needs the gates, and the honest disposition is `duplicate`
naming aec1 as the live replacement — which is exactly the disposition-attestation path
[rebar:738a-376e-4829-42ca] fixed earlier in this epic. Recording the relationship now so neither
ticket is worked twice.

compiled_state.description:
# A gate whose spend is never recorded cannot be tuned: per-run request/tool-call counts are not persisted

Discovered while root-causing [rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e]. The operator asked a simple, decisive
question about the completion gate: **how many model requests did the epics that PASSED this gate
actually consume?** That question is the control group for "is e369 abnormal, or is the budget
just too small?" — and it **cannot be answered from anything this system records.**

## What is actually recorded (checked in both directions, not assumed)

* `usage_log.record()` (`src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:259-318`) appends one JSONL row per LLM call —
  but **only to `$REBAR_USAGE_LOG`, and it is a no-op when that env var is unset**, which is the
  default: *"No-op when the env var is unset (the default) or `usage` is empty."* It is unset in this
  environment and is documented with no default (`docs/env-vars.md:152`). So by default **no per-run
  spend record is written at all.**
* Even with the opt-in enabled, the recorded fields are
  `_FIELDS = ("input_tokens", "output_tokens", "cache_read_tokens", "cache_write_tokens", "requests")`
  (`usage_log.py:32`). **`tool_calls` is not among them** — and `tool_calls` is precisely the axis
  that (a) discriminates a loop from genuine breadth and (b) is the SECOND, independent kill path
  (`tool_calls_limit`, `structured_run.py:399-412`) that `requests` cannot see.
* The signed attestation records the verdict, not the cost: the completion sidecar
  (`rebar audit show <id> --output json` -> `completion.sidecar`) carries criteria and citations and
  **no request or tool-call counts**; `completion.attestation.step_count` is WORKFLOW steps (7), not
  model requests.
* Nothing is on disk to fall back to: `.rebar/logs/` contains only `enrich-drain.log` (0 bytes).

## The asymmetry that makes it worse

`usage_log.failure_usage` (`usage_log.py:136-190`) DOES compute `tool_calls` plus the full repetition
summary — but only on the **failure** path, and [rebar:8b97-a0ca-82a4-4d4e] shows that value is then
discarded one frame from the surface. So:

* a run that **fails** computes rich spend/repetition data and throws it away;
* a run that **succeeds** never computes it at all.

The net effect is that the gate's cost profile is invisible in both directions. This is the same
"computed then discarded" shape as the dropped diagnostic, one level up: not a missing metric, but a
**missing durable record of what the gate actually spent**.

## Why it blocks real decisions

Concretely, during [rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e] these questions were all unanswerable retrospectively
and had to be replaced with ~70 minutes of fresh instrumented live re-runs:

* how many requests did `2f4c` / `a492` / `86ac` / `716f` / `e68d` consume when they PASSED?
* is e369's consumption abnormal, or in line with them?
* has per-run spend trended up as the runtime changed (LangChain -> pydantic-ai, budget raises)?

The only available proxy was realized-evidence volume reconstructed from the sidecars (criteria
count and distinct cited files: 3-9 criteria, 2-9 files), which measures the OUTPUT, not the spend.

## Scope

Observability only. This ticket does not propose changing any budget, gate or verdict.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a durable per-run record of LLM spend for gate runs exists WITHOUT requiring an operator to
      have set an env var beforehand — a gate's own spend must be recoverable after the fact
- [ ] the record includes `tool_calls` alongside `requests`, since the two ceilings are independent
      and only `tool_calls` can distinguish a loop from breadth
- [ ] the record is written for BOTH outcomes — a successful verification and a failed one — so a
      control group of passing runs exists to compare a failing run against
- [ ] the record is attributable to the ticket and the gate that ran, so "what did the completion
      gate spend on ticket X" is answerable
- [ ] the privacy contract of `usage_log` is unchanged: counters and hashed signatures only, never
      prompt/response/tool-argument content
- [ ] a test pins that a gate run leaves a retrievable spend record with `requests` and `tool_calls`
      populated
compiled_state.title: Gate spend is never durably recorded: per-run request/tool-call counts unavailable after the fact
